pull.title: KAFKA-20895: Grant pre-vote once the leader has resigned
pull.body:
## Summary

`FollowerState.canGrantVote()` rejects a pre-vote whenever
`hasFetchedFromLeader` is true, ignoring that the leader may have
already announced it is resigning. On a clean shutdown the first
preferred successor then collects only its own vote plus the resigned
leader's, which is not a majority once the quorum is larger than three,
so it loses and a lower-ranked node wins instead. Every graceful
controller shutdown wastes an election round.

The fix lets a follower know its leader has stepped down, and treats
that as grounds to grant a pre-vote:

- `FollowerState` gains a `hasLeaderResigned` flag and a
`setHasLeaderResigned()` setter.
- `KafkaRaftClient.handleEndQuorumEpochRequest()` calls that setter next
to the existing `overrideFetchTimeout()`, inside the block already
guarded by "still a follower" and "the request came from our own
leader". The flag is only set on a genuine resignation from the leader
we are following.
- The grant condition becomes `isPreVote && (!hasFetchedFromLeader ||
hasLeaderResigned) && isLogUpToDate`. Standard votes are unchanged.

## Test plan

- `FollowerStateTest.testPreVoteAfterLeaderResigned`: after a successful
fetch, a pre-vote is granted only when the leader has resigned and the
requester's log is up to date. A standard vote is still rejected.
-
`KafkaRaftClientPreVoteTest.testFollowerGrantsPreVoteAfterLeaderResigns`:
the follower fetches from the leader and rejects a pre-vote from an
up-to-date peer. It then receives an `EndQuorumEpochRequest` from that
leader and grants the same pre-vote. The test runs once, on
`KIP_1186_PROTOCOL`.

The earlier `RaftEventSimulationTest` case was removed. This behavior is
covered by the unit tests above.

Reviewers: Kevin Wu <kwu@confluent.io>

review_comments.body: Should we have a test for that change in `FollowerStateTest`?
Sure thing. Added. Please check

I do not think we should have a simulation test for this. This issue is more of a performance issue, whereas the simulation tests are conceptually more about ensuring the invariants of the KRaft protocol are upheld. Additionally, simulation tests are more expensive to run than the unit tests. For example, this test could fail if you decided to drop some messages, which happens in the real world a lot.

See my other comment for how you can make the unit test model this situation without using a simulation test.

In my opinion, a better test would have the local follower node start as rejecting preVotes from a remote node whose log is up to date because `hasFetchedFromLeader` is true. Then, the follower is delivered an `EndQuorumEpochRequest` to model the leader resigning. Finally, this test should show that a preVote is now granted by the local follower. 

Writing a unit test like this also makes it so we do not need the simulation test below IMO. It would go in `KafkaRaftClientPreVoteTest`.

What do you think?
nit: `setHasLeaderResigned`

nit: can we reword this slightly? I would prefer not using 'stand for election one at a time' as it gives the impression of strict 'one after the other'. maybe something like:
```
Keep the larger, default quorum.election.backoff.max.ms here to give successors enough time to be 
considered one after another. This config sets how long each successor waits before it starts an election. 
With a small value it is more likely two successors will have overlapping elections.
```
do we need this? seems to be covered by the assert below
also if the calculation were to change in the production code then this becomes out of date
why not use `withVotersObservers`?
do we need this change?

Agreed. I added testFollowerGrantsPreVoteAfterLeaderResigns to KafkaRaftClientPreVoteTest. After a successful fetch, the follower rejects a PreVote from an up-to-date node. It then receives an EndQuorumEpochRequest from the leader and grants the same PreVote. I kept the FollowerStateTest case as a state-level check, since Mickael asked for it. Happy to drop it if you'd prefer.
Makes sense, thanks. I removed the simulation test and replaced it with a unit test in KafkaRaftClientPreVoteTest.
No longer applicable. The simulation test was removed in favour of the unit test.
Thanks. Per Kevin's feedback, this simulation test has been removed, so the comment is gone too.
Good point. That calculation is gone now that the simulation test has been removed.
Removed along with the simulation test.
Reverted. It was only needed by the simulation test, so RaftEventSimulationTest now matches trunk.

> I kept the FollowerStateTest case as a state-level check, since Mickael asked for it.

Yeah that is fine to keep.
We do not need to parametrize over the `kraftVersion`. That feature and pre-vote are not related.
Please use the most recent value for `RaftProtocol`. That contains pre-vote too.

It might be good to store `context.preVoteRequest` in a variable. That way, it is clear to the test reader that the same pre-vote request first gets rejected, and then after the leader resigns, the same request now gets granted.
What is the motivation behind checking that the local node is a follower repeatedly?
A PreVote response does not change the node's role, so those checks were unnecessary. I kept only the check after EndQuorumEpoch, because that request can move the node out of the follower state.
Agree. Stored the PreVote request and reused it, so the rejected and granted requests are the same object.
Switched the test to KIP_1186_PROTOCOL, the latest protocol, which still includes pre-vote.
Please add this empty line back to pass the checkstyle.
Added the blank line back.

```suggestion
        assertEquals(
            isLogUpToDate, 
            state.canGrantVote(ReplicaKey.of(1, ReplicaKey.NO_DIRECTORY_ID), isLogUpToDate, true)
        );
```
There is a convention in the `raft` module to keep lines under 100 characters in length. This applies to many places in this PR.
Updated.
Wrapped the new lines so they stay under 100 characters.

commit.message:
KAFKA-20895: Grant pre-vote once the leader has resigned

On a clean shutdown the leader sends EndQuorumEpoch carrying a list of
preferred successors ordered by log end offset, and each successor waits a
backoff proportional to its position before standing for election. The
first entry, being the most up to date, is expected to win.

It cannot. FollowerState.canGrantVote() rejects a pre-vote whenever
hasFetchedFromLeader is true, without accounting for the leader having
already announced that it is resigning. With more than three voters the
first successor collects only its own vote and the resigned leader's,
which is not a majority, so it loses and returns to follower. The second
entry then wins, because by that point the first entry has transitioned
away from follower and is able to vote. The pattern repeats for larger
quorums: the third entry wins with six or seven voters, the fourth with
eight or nine. Every graceful controller shutdown therefore wastes an
election round.

Track whether the leader of the current epoch has resigned, and let a
follower grant a pre-vote in that case even if it has already fetched, as
long as the requester's log is up to date. Granting is no longer
disruptive once the leader has stepped down. Standard votes are
unaffected.

Add a multi-node simulation covering quorums of four through nine voters,
which asserts that the first preferred successor becomes the new leader.
Without this change it fails for every one of those quorum sizes, with the
winner landing at exactly the position the JIRA predicts.

KAFKA-20895: Add FollowerState unit test for granting pre-vote after resignation

Cover the canGrantVote() change directly, in addition to the existing
multi-node simulation. The test puts a follower in the state a graceful
shutdown produces, having already fetched from the leader and then having
received the leader's resignation, and asserts a pre-vote is granted only
when the requester's log is up to date. It also asserts standard votes are
still rejected, so the new flag cannot widen that path.

Without the production change the up-to-date case fails.

KAFKA-20895: Address review comments on pre-vote after leader resignation

- Rename FollowerState#setLeaderHasResigned to setHasLeaderResigned
- Add KafkaRaftClientPreVoteTest#testFollowerGrantsPreVoteAfterLeaderResigns,
  which checks that a follower rejects a PreVote after fetching from the
  leader and grants it once it receives EndQuorumEpoch from that leader
- Remove the RaftEventSimulationTest case and its electionBackoffMaxMs
  field in favour of the unit test

KAFKA-20895: Adjust the pre-vote-after-resignation test for review

Run the test once on the latest Raft protocol instead of every KRaft version, and reuse one PreVote request for both the rejection and the grant.

KAFKA-20895: Restore the import-group blank line in the pre-vote test

Checkstyle requires a blank line between the Kafka imports and the JUnit imports.

KAFKA-20895: Keep the new raft test lines under 100 characters

Wrap the assertions and comments added for the pre-vote-after-resignation tests, and spell out why the follower stays a follower after EndQuorumEpoch.
